platforms.title: The First Time the Bible Says Finished, Nothing Was Broken
platforms.description:
It is finished (John 19:30). But the FIRST time the Bible says finished, nothing was broken yet: thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them (Genesis 2:1). Creation complete. God rested. He does not leave work half done.

When sin wrecked that world, the Son came down to mend it. All things were made by him; the hands that finished creation came to finish redemption.

"When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost" (John 19:30, KJV).

Two finished works. One Workman. He finished creation and rested; he finished redemption and rested in the tomb through the sabbath. And on the first day, morning came.

You were never asked to finish it. You are asked to rest in it. He bowed his head so you could lift yours. The work is finished. Enter his rest.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: It Is Finished: Two Finished Works, One Workman
platforms.description:
The most famous last words in history are three words from a cross (John 19:30): it is finished. But the Bible has said finished before, and the first time, nothing was broken yet.

"Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them" (Genesis 2:1). Creation complete, and God rested. He does not leave work half done.

When sin wrecked that finished world, the Son came down to mend it. Scripture says of Jesus: all things were made by him. The same hands that finished creation came to finish redemption. On the night before the cross he prayed, "I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do" (John 17:4). And he carried it to the end:

"When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost" (John 19:30, KJV).

Two finished works. One Workman. He finished creation, and rested on the seventh day. He finished redemption, and rested in the tomb through the sabbath. And on the first day of the week, morning came.

In this piece: the Genesis rhyme behind the cross's greatest word, the prayer of John 17, and the invitation folded inside it all: you were never asked to finish the work. You are asked to rest in it.

He bowed his head so you could lift yours. Enter his rest.
